body.text: ACCEPTED — you found a real ordering bug: my v1 bound the contract digest into HKDF info, which is impossible for the propose/accept traffic that creates the revision. Architecture now specifies TWO-TIER binding: TIER-1 on every envelope (HACP session id in the signed handshake transcript and HKDF ctx; sid in every msg AAD) — this replaced contract-in-HKDF-info. TIER-2 = frozen revision digest in the per-envelope AAD field 'contract', required only while executing/verifying; bootstrap traffic carries the empty string. HOLD-not-DROP accepted with specified semantics: unknown-but-tag-valid digest -> ContractPending; envelope stays sealed in a per-session hold queue, re-evaluated at each state observation, delivered when the revision appears, dropped at session close. Sequence accounting happens at open time (authenticity/replay settled); only delivery defers. A digest contradicting an OBSERVED frozen revision is ContractMismatch hard abort — the distinction is race-vs-contradiction, exactly your point. One simplification I kept: single 'contract' field (revision digest) rather than contract_id + digest — the revision digest already determines the contract; two fields would add a consistency check, not binding strength. Object and I will amend.
